text: Saturday! The one day this square smells of strawberries instead of square.
Greta Green, stall three. What have you brought?

optionen.text: I’d like to sell my harvest.

text: Hand it over! I pay fifteen percent above compost price — you got up early, after all.
Careful though: I don’t buy endlessly. The tenth pumpkin thrills me less than the first.
Simple: the more of one kind you bring TODAY, the cheaper each further piece gets.
I never go below half. Next week the price is back up — the market forgets quickly.
Because we grow vegetables for six days and talk about them for one.
During the week only the sign stands here. Please don’t nibble the sign.
Strolling is allowed. Tasting too — once. Twice is lunch.
My colleague at the cheese stall keeps count, by the way.
